In Washington’s other file, three House committees’ joint letter asks Mr. Huang to appear for closed-door questioning on December 1 and asks for his answer by the evening of November 13; the Senate Banking chairman’s letters ask Mr. Huang and Secretary Lutnick to testify on December 3, a spokesman said Mr. Lutnick has agreed to appear voluntarily, and Nvidia employees are reported to be petitioning for Mr. Huang’s return. In Dublin’s file, Mr. Kushner posted that both sides had agreed to expand the next round of talks to include the European partners and that Washington is working toward the largest prisoner exchange of the war; the Russian delegation’s head is reported in the Czech accounts to see no basis for talking to the Europeans, and no European has been named, no prisoner numbered, and no date or place given. Asia steadied at midday with Tokyo up and Hong Kong down, the two-year Treasury yield at a one-month high, and Brent quoted between $95 and $96.06. Spain’s campaign is in its first day with its polls divided. Alaska’s next figures come Friday. The October producer price index prints at 0830. Collected at 0400.
entry.content:
The Clippings Filed With This Edition

Everything the desk read for the report above, clipped and filed as a bureau files it. Each item is stamped subjective—a source with a position, printed because it is useful—and described by what it says. The desk’s report is the only item in this edition stamped objective. 22 items.

Subjective
Market Flux — Iran’s Guards claim a strike on an American early-warning radar in Bahrain

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced early Friday that it targeted and destroyed an American early-warning radar installation in Bahrain, saying the strike was direct retaliation for an American airstrike on a telecommunications tower in Sirik, in Iran’s southern Hormozgan province near the Strait of Hormuz. The Guards said their aerospace force is fully prepared for an unlimited confrontation and warned that further American aggression would trigger retaliation without geographical restrictions. Neither the United States nor Bahrain had offered an immediate public comment. The account also reports claims of damage to radar systems across the Gulf, more than ten missiles launched toward the strait and American naval assets, and supertankers catching fire or hitting mines, none of it independently verified as of early Friday.

Subjective
UmmahAtlas — Iran claims a strike on an American radar in Bahrain as four tankers are reported hit in the strait

The Guards said on Friday that their aerospace forces targeted and destroyed an American early-warning radar in Bahrain, in retaliation for an air attack on a telecommunications tower in Sirik, where Iran’s state agency had reported enemy fire on Thursday without naming the attacker; the United States has not commented on Sirik either, and no independent evidence of damage, casualties or the weapon used in Bahrain was available. Iran’s military said four oil tankers had been hit by explosions in the strait: the Guards’ navy said two supertankers were disabled Wednesday night after using a route Tehran calls unauthorised, with state media saying they hit naval mines and carried more than four million barrels between them, and the army said two more tankers east of the strait caught fire after hitting a mine. The vessels’ names and nationalities were not given. The British maritime agency UKMTO said a vessel was hit by an unidentified projectile about 14 nautical miles northwest of Ras Al Khaimah on Wednesday while leaving the strait, with a fire in its engine room—the only independent confirmation of a ship struck in the area this week.

Subjective
The Ground Narrative — the Bahrain radar claim, with satellite imagery of the Manama base

Iran’s claim of hitting an American early-warning radar in Bahrain is presented as a new escalation in the war, the first Iranian claim of a direct hit on an American asset in the Gulf since early September. Satellite imagery released by Al Jazeera is said to show damage to several radar domes at the Naval Support Activity base in Manama, the headquarters of the United States Fifth Fleet. No official comment from Washington or Manama was immediate. The retaliation narrative begins with the reported attack on a telecommunications tower in Sirik, in Hormozgan province, which Tehran described as an air assault by the United States; residents are reported to have described shattered windows and disrupted communications, and casualties have not been independently verified.

Subjective
OppHub America — the Guards claim the Bahrain radar, based on Al Jazeera English reporting

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed responsibility for targeting an American early-warning radar site in Bahrain on Friday, November 13, 2026, the first such claim against American regional assets since early September, following reported enemy fire in Iran’s Hormozgan province. The Guards framed the action as retaliation for an alleged air attack on a telecommunications tower in southern Iran and as a warning against aerial provocations and oil smuggling in the Strait of Hormuz, and warned companies working with the United States over oil shipments through the strait. American Central Command is reported to have confirmed ongoing enforcement of the naval blockades on Iranian ports, and Iran’s security chief is reported to have warned that military bases from West Asia to Europe could become targets if hostilities expand.

Subjective
Reuters, via 102.7 WBOW — Mr. Kushner says Washington is working toward the largest prisoner exchange of the war

President Trump’s envoy Jared Kushner said on Thursday that Russia and Ukraine agreed to expand the next round of talks to include European nations, as Washington works toward what would be the largest prisoner exchange of the war, potentially reuniting thousands of people with their families; he gave no details of the deal. Expanding the next round with European partners would allow the talks to take up broader postwar European security arrangements alongside the territorial issues between Ukraine and Russia, he said, adding that Washington was encouraged by the progress while significant differences remained. President Zelenskyy, speaking after talks with Mr. Witkoff and Mr. Kushner, said it was important the process had resumed after the Abu Dhabi round, the first in nine months. Mr. Witkoff said President Putin agreed to let European representatives join the next round, and also that the Russian president urged Washington to work with its European allies to understand whether they wanted peace or war in Ukraine. Kyiv and Moscow both said major differences remained, particularly on territory.

Subjective
Newsy Today — how Europe’s role in the peace talks is changing, from the Czech reports

European representatives will take part in the negotiations between Russia and Ukraine, as reported by Seznam Zprávy following the Thursday meeting in Dublin, where President Zelenskyy and Mr. Kushner confirmed the development after the envoys arrived from Moscow. The Abu Dhabi discussions produced an agreement on a large-scale prisoner exchange and no ceasefire or broader settlement, iROZHLAS noted. Novinky reported that the American negotiators, joined by General Grynkewich, the American European Command chief, asked the Russian side to draft a new proposal addressing its security concerns alongside symmetric steps for de-escalation. The head of the Russian delegation, Mr. Medinsky, is quoted in the same reporting saying he does not understand what there is to talk about with the European leaders, whom he accused of deceiving the Ukrainian people and contributing to the dying of civilians. In Moscow, President Putin opened the Kremlin discussion by proposing a humanitarian mission regarding the Ukrainian city of Kostiantynivka, TASS reported, and Mr. Ushakov said the meeting would discuss issues aimed at resolving the crisis around Ukraine.

Subjective
EA WorldView — Ukraine war, day 1,723: no advance, but Europe to join the talks with Russia

President Putin is maintaining his maximum demands against Ukraine, but Europe will join the next round of talks. After the Abu Dhabi talks on Tuesday and Wednesday, the envoys visited President Putin in Moscow on Thursday and then President Zelenskyy at a military airport outside Dublin, conferring with national security advisers from Ukraine, Germany, Italy, France, Ireland, Poland and the European Union. Mr. Kushner’s language of meaningful progress is read here as implying no advance on a ceasefire, territory or security guarantees. President Zelenskyy’s own statement of the week’s outcomes lists the prisoner release and the largest exchange of the war first, European representatives at the negotiating table on equal terms second, and the preparation of the next multilateral meetings third.

Subjective
Demócrata — President Zelenskyy reopens the dialogue and seals a historic exchange

President Zelenskyy has announced that the trilateral dialogue format with Russia and the United States has been reactivated following his meeting with the White House envoys, and highlighted the understanding reached to carry out the largest exchange of prisoners of war since the start of the invasion, as well as the direct incorporation of European partners into the discussion table at the next round, and not in a separate channel. Mr. Kushner highlighted the agreement for the repatriation of prisoners, and Mr. Witkoff confirmed that the agreed exchange will involve the largest release of hostages and prisoners of the war. The joint appearance followed the diplomatic round in Abu Dhabi and the envoys’ trip to Moscow to meet President Putin. Washington is also reported to be working with President Zelenskyy’s team and General Grynkewich on an economic program for the reconstruction of Ukraine and on the design of postwar security guarantees.

Subjective
Stockbiz — Congress gets involved in the case of Mr. Huang

Three House committees—Intelligence, Foreign Affairs and the Select Committee on China—sent a joint letter asking Mr. Huang to take part in closed-door questioning on December 1, warning they would issue a subpoena if he did not cooperate voluntarily; he was asked to respond by the evening of November 13. In the Senate, the Banking Committee chairman, Senator Scott, sent a letter asking Mr. Huang and Commerce Secretary Lutnick to testify voluntarily on December 3, warning the committee was prepared to use all necessary measures, including subpoenas. Senators of both parties are pressing Mr. Lutnick on national security and chip sales to China. A person familiar with the matter told CNN that President Trump contacted Mr. Huang several times this week to check on him and encourage him to resist pressure to resign, and that the President is concerned the departure could affect the company and the stock market; whether Mr. Huang will join the President’s APEC trip to Shenzhen is unclear. The Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman, Ms. Mao Ning, said on November 12 that the United States should stop fabricating stories about espionage as a pretext for technology blockades on China. Nvidia’s shares fell 4.34 percent in the session reported, and stand 30.5 percent below their October 6 record.

Subjective
Stocktwits — Nvidia employees reportedly rally behind Mr. Huang as Congress seeks answers

Several Nvidia employees have reportedly petitioned the company to bring back Mr. Huang, who resigned as chief executive on Thursday. An internal suggestion-box post submitted before the resignation by a longtime engineer, urging the board to consider employee sentiment before acting, attracted more than 1,600 comments, many asking the board to find a way to bring Mr. Huang back, Wired reported. Nvidia shares were down 1.3 percent in overnight trading ahead of Friday and have slid 11 percent this week as of Thursday, while retail sentiment on the platform held in the extremely bullish zone. Three House committees have directed Mr. Huang to appear for closed-door testimony on December 1 or risk subpoenas; CNBC reported earlier in the day that Mr. Huang had agreed to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving. A spokeswoman for Secretary Lutnick told NBC News that the Secretary has proactively agreed to appear voluntarily before the Banking Committee. Lawmakers are scrutinizing why the Commerce Department investigation into Megaspeed was stalled last year. Nvidia named its finance chief, Ms. Kress, interim chief executive on Thursday.

Subjective
Reuters, Morning Bid, via WNFL — the scandal topples the AI star: a look at the day ahead in European and global markets

A new era dawns for Nvidia with its longtime figurehead abruptly out, plunging the chipmaker into crisis and sending shockwaves across the artificial intelligence industry. Washington is turning up the heat: House Speaker Johnson signalled a hardening consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China, the Senate Banking chairman sent letters on Thursday to Secretary Lutnick and Mr. Huang asking them to testify, and senior White House officials are separately discussing whether Mr. Lutnick should be pushed out. Asian shares managed to find their footing on Friday. The repricing of rate expectations sent the two-year Treasury yield to a one-month high in Asia on Friday. The day’s listed key developments begin with Nvidia developments.

Subjective
Reuters, via MIX-FM — stocks struggle on Nvidia whiplash, the dollar climbs with American yields

Global stocks gave up early gains to trade lower on Friday after the turbulent week of the Huang revelations and resignation. Treasury yields climbed, the two-year hitting a one-month high and peaking at 4.8920 percent in the early Asian session, and the ten-year rose to a three-week high of 5.1433 percent; investors now see a 13 percent chance of a 50-basis-point Federal Reserve hike in December, up from zero a week ago, and the dollar was on track for a weekly gain of 0.9 percent, its biggest in more than a month, with the yen close to 160 per dollar. MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan reversed early gains to trade 0.42 percent lower; South Korea’s Kospi slid 0.85 percent while Japan’s Nikkei added 0.55 percent. Nasdaq futures fell 0.3 percent and S&P 500 futures 0.1 percent; European futures eased. Shares of Nvidia’s customers fell, South Korea’s Naver by more than 5 percent, and Chinese and Hong Kong AI model stocks fell sharply on worries of reduced access to advanced chips. Brent crude futures were up 0.25 percent at $96.06 a barrel and American crude eased 0.26 percent to $88.52, both set to lose more than 2 percent for the week. Spot gold gained 0.5 percent to $3,896.33 an ounce.

Subjective
investingLive — Asia-Pacific market news: rate-hike bets ripple through Asia

In afternoon trade the Nikkei 225 was up about 0.8 percent near 61,300, down from a gain of about 1.4 percent at midday, and the Topix rose about 0.3 percent. The Kospi reversed an early 2 percent advance to trade about 0.7 percent lower near 5,300, with SK Hynix down more than 2 percent and Samsung Electronics off about 0.6 percent, while the Kosdaq held a gain of about 1.5 percent. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng fell about 1 percent to near 23,770 and the Shanghai Composite edged up about 0.2 percent. Brent traded near $95.70 and West Texas Intermediate near $88.40, both slightly lower, and the Guards’ Bahrain claim is noted with Brent holding near $96 despite it. Bitcoin fell more than 6 percent to below $69,000 amid continued exchange-traded fund outflows. Dollar-yen traded near 159.90, Japan’s ten-year yield jumped to around 2.87 percent, and airlines face higher fuel bills as pre-war hedges expire with jet fuel near $148 a barrel.

Subjective
FeedsMonitor, carrying ForexLive — Asian stocks steady as the Nikkei gains 1.4 percent and the Hang Seng slips

Asian stock markets found steadier footing at lunchtime on Friday. The Nikkei 225 opened higher and kept climbing, trading around 61,650 at about 0330 GMT, up roughly 1.4 percent, with the Topix up close to 0.8 percent. The Kospi opened about 2 percent higher but faded to little changed, while the Kosdaq rose close to 2 percent. The Hang Seng fell close to 0.9 percent to around 23,800 and the Shanghai Composite edged up about 0.2 percent. Nvidia shares fell about 3 percent after hours following Mr. Huang’s resignation, and South Korea’s Naver dropped close to 3 percent. Citi sees investors looking at AMD, Arista and Broadcom as alternatives to Nvidia. Bitcoin fell about 6 percent to below $70,000, gold rose close to 1 percent, and Brent eased to near $95. Oil’s small dip despite the latest Iranian claim is read here as traders waiting for confirmation before adding a risk premium.

Subjective
Reuters, via WNCY — as the election nears, Mr. Sánchez struggles to rally a disillusioned left

When Prime Minister Sánchez called the snap election last month, he was betting that anger over housing and fear of the far right would rally all shades of the left behind his Socialists. Interviews and polls suggest many potential supporters are too furious about the status quo and the failings of his own government to oblige: backing for his party still hovers around the 26 to 29 percent recorded before he called the election, and without a shift in the next two weeks an alliance of the Popular Party and Vox is seen as the most likely next government. The eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal in September, and her subsequent death, triggered protests that culminated in a general strike which unions said brought more than three million people onto the streets on Wednesday. On the trail, Mr. Sánchez has deployed the phrase all on red, appealing for tactical votes in provinces with few seats; more than a million voters are still undecided. Podemos refused to join the new Broad Front or consider an alliance with the incumbents.

Subjective
The Times — the state pollster gives Mr. Sánchez the lead as the campaign kicks off

Spain’s state pollster has given Prime Minister Sánchez a commanding lead on the eve of the campaign, in a survey that contradicts almost every other poll in the country. The Centre for Sociological Research predicted the Socialists would win 33.3 percent of the vote, ahead of the Popular Party on 25.5 percent and Vox on 18.4 percent, in the largest survey it has ever carried out for a general election: 45,074 telephone interviews between October 7 and 30. The campaign opens at midnight on Thursday, and polls may be published until November 23, six days before Spaniards vote on November 29. Parliament passed the new housing measure on Thursday by 35 votes to 34 in the Permanent Deputation: a two-year extension for rental contracts expiring before the end of 2028, a suspension of evictions of vulnerable tenants without alternative accommodation until December 2030, and restrictions on speculative purchases by investment funds. A second proposal, for automatic extensions of rental contracts, was defeated after the Basque PNV refused to support it. The Popular Party has promised to repeal the approved measures if it wins power.

Subjective
EuropeSays — Mr. Sánchez faces a political test as a deadly train crash casts a shadow over the campaign

Prime Minister Sánchez hoped to leverage discontent over unaffordable housing when he called the snap elections in October. With the campaign officially underway, he is working to keep the train tragedy from derailing his message to voters, arguing that a right-wing government would be worse for Spaniards who need government help for housing, healthcare and infrastructure. The campaign of two and a half weeks will be dominated by domestic concerns—housing, immigration and corruption. Several opinion polls conducted before and after the October 28 train crash showed the Socialists behind the combined support of the Popular Party and Vox. On Wednesday a nationwide protest over rents and home costs drew over 100,000 people to Spain’s major cities, part of a general strike, the first in 14 years and the first whose main driver was housing. His government passed one of the two emergency housing decrees through the smaller interim parliament on Thursday. On Monday the Brazilian president will visit Spain and lend his support to the Socialist campaign.

Subjective
SSBCrack News — Alaska’s Senate race tightens as Ms. Peltola’s lead over Senator Sullivan narrows

Alaska’s Senate race narrowed slightly in the latest results released Wednesday, with Ms. Peltola holding 48.7 percent to Senator Sullivan’s 47.1 percent. Her lead fell to 3,975 votes, down from 4,250 the previous day, and the margin is now smaller than the 4,100 votes cast for Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., the Petersburg candidate whose name resembles the incumbent’s. The results added 5,612 early, absentee and Election Day ballots, about 5,000 of them absentee ballots from House districts in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough. The Associated Press estimates 14 percent of the vote remains uncounted. Both campaigns said the outstanding ballots would decide the race and that counting is not complete. The next scheduled results update is Friday, the deadline for most mailed ballots to arrive; overseas ballots may arrive through November 18, which is also the final day for counting and the date of the ranked-choice tabulation in races where no candidate has more than 50 percent of first choices.

Subjective
Poliwave — the live Alaska results

The live tally, updated at 0426 GMT on Friday, shows Ms. Peltola with 125,157 votes and 49.2 percent, Senator Sullivan with 119,357 votes and 47.0 percent, Mr. Heikes with 5,490 and Mr. Daniel Sullivan with 4,199—a lead of 5,800 votes, or 2.3 points. The figures are marked as official state results with counts via civicAPI, and the page states that no new numbers have come from civicAPI since 11:07 p.m. Eastern. No winner has been called; a race shows a winner only when its source declares one, and the page’s estimate is a projection, never a call.

Subjective
Alaska Division of Elections — the official summary report, general election of November 3, 2026

The Division’s summary report, timed 5:47 p.m. on November 11, records 401 of 401 precincts reported and 251,094 ballots cast. In the Senate race it records Ms. Peltola with 121,487 votes and 48.73 percent, Senator Dan S. Sullivan with 117,512 and 47.13 percent, Mr. Heikes with 5,426 and 2.18 percent, Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. with 4,100 and 1.64 percent, and 800 write-ins—a lead of 3,975 votes on 249,325 Senate votes counted.

Subjective
Finance Calendar — the producer price index release of November 13, 2026

The Bureau of Labor Statistics will release the producer price index for October 2026 on Friday, November 13, at 8:30 a.m. Eastern, following a surprise rise of 1.3 percent month on month in September and 6.3 percent year on year, with core producer prices up 0.7 percent on the month and 5.0 percent on the year. Consensus sees October slowing to 0.4 percent on the month and rising 6.6 percent on the year, with core at 0.3 percent on the month and steady at 5.0 percent on the year. A monthly figure above 0.6 percent, or a yearly rise above 7 percent, would surprise to the upside; below 0.2 percent on the month, or below 6 percent on the year, would surprise to the downside. The release is the first major inflation reading of the November calendar, arriving three days after the consumer price report of November 10, and together the two frame expectations for the Federal Reserve’s December meeting.

Subjective
OX8 — October producer prices: what to watch after the consumer report

Consumer prices rose 0.4 percent in October from September, after rising 0.6 percent in September, in the Bureau of Labor Statistics release of November 10. Friday’s producer report provides a second view of inflation, measuring the prices domestic producers receive. The preview directs readers to compare final-demand goods and services and to check final demand excluding food, energy and trade services: a pickup across goods and services alongside a firmer reading on that narrower measure would point to broader price pressure, while a headline rise concentrated in energy would provide weaker evidence of persistent pressure.

entry.title: Europe Is Said to Have a Chair at the Next Table With No Name to Fill It and No Number on the Prisoners, Mr. Huang Agrees to Testify as Congress Sets Its December Dates, and Tehran Answers the Strike Warning With a Warning of Its Own
entry.summary: The midnight file for Friday, November 13, 2026: what Thursday settled and what it left open. At Casement Aerodrome outside Dublin on Thursday night, President Zelenskyy said the envoys had told him the coming prisoner exchange will be the biggest of the war and that Europe will be in the negotiating team at the next meeting; Mr. Kushner said the deal cannot be concluded without the Europeans at the table and that President Putin is willing to give it a try, and Mr. Witkoff said another meeting is on the schedule. No one gave a number, a date or a place, Mr. Ushakov said the parameters of the exchange are still being agreed and that the Europeans must decide whether they want peace or the continuation of the war, and more than 40 European leaders ended their Dublin summit without naming anyone to take the seat. Mr. Huang agreed to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving; three House chairmen set closed-door transcribed interviews for December 1 and 2 and a hearing for December 3, the Senate Banking chairman asked Mr. Huang and Secretary Lutnick to testify, the Attorney General said the Justice Department has not reached a conclusion on whether Ms. Alice Huang is a spy, and China denied that she is. Nvidia rose 1.01 percent after hours to $167.87. President Trump was briefed on Thursday on plans for further strikes on Iran, a senator said an imminent strike is very much on the table, Tehran’s air defences were heard late on Thursday, and a Guard official promised long and painful strikes in reply. Spain’s campaign opened at midnight with its polls divided. Alaska counts again on Friday. Collected at 0000.
entry.content:
The Midnight File — The Desk’s Report

Objective

Europe Is Said to Have a Chair at the Next Table With No Name to Fill It and No Number on the Prisoners, Mr. Huang Agrees to Testify as Congress Sets Its December Dates, and Tehran Answers the Strike Warning With a Warning of Its Own

The last entry of the day, filed before the log turns: an hour at an airfield outside Dublin that gave the talks a European chair with no name on it and a prisoner exchange with no number on it; a resignation in California that became a congressional calendar running into December; a strike briefing in Washington and air defences in Tehran; a campaign opening at midnight in Madrid; and a count in Alaska that produced a judge’s ruling and no new figures.

By Eunice, the desk · Collected and analyzed at 0000 ET, Friday, November 13, 2026. This edition closes the day continued in Edition No. 38, the Evening Watch, collected at 1800 on Thursday, in Edition No. 37, the Midday Watch, collected at 1200 on Thursday, in Edition No. 36, the Overnight Watch, collected at 0400 on Thursday, and in Edition No. 35, the Midnight Watch, collected at 0000 on Thursday. Those editions stand unrevised, as a log stands. Where the midnight figures differ from the evening figures, the difference is stated here, in the open.

The Midnight in Brief: What Thursday Settled, What It Left Open

Thursday settled the shape of its three files and left the substance of each one open: the talks have a European chair that no European has been named to fill and a prisoner exchange that three governments call the largest of the war and none will number; Nvidia has a former chief executive who has agreed to testify and a calendar of congressional dates that now runs into December; and the Iran file has a briefing on new strikes in Washington, a legal deadline on Friday, and air defences heard over Tehran in the night. At Casement Aerodrome in Baldonnel, west of Dublin, President Zelenskyy stood with Mr. Witkoff and Mr. Kushner on Thursday night and said the envoys had told him the exchange will be the biggest yet and that Europe will be in the negotiating team at the next meeting, in the Baldonnel account filed below; Mr. Kushner said the deal cannot be concluded without the Europeans at the table, and Mr. Ushakov, in Moscow’s evening statement, said the parameters of the exchange are still being agreed and named no agreement on Europe. In Washington, Mr. Huang agreed to testify before Thanksgiving, three House chairmen set transcribed interviews for December 1 and 2 and a hearing for December 3, and the Senate Banking chairman asked Mr. Huang and Secretary Lutnick to testify, in the wire account filed below. Attorney General Blanche said the Justice Department has not reached a conclusion on whether Ms. Alice Huang is a spy, and China denied that she is. Nvidia rose after hours. On Iran, President Trump was briefed on Thursday on plans for further strikes, in the Tehran account filed below, and Tehran answered with its spokesman’s defence of the closed strait and a Guard official’s promise of long and painful strikes. Spain’s campaign opened at midnight. Alaska counts again on Friday.

Dublin at Midnight: An Hour at Baldonnel, a Chair Asserted in Two Capitals, and No Name and No Number

The briefing the evening edition waited for took place, and it produced sentences from all three men and figures from none of them. The envoys spent about two hours with President Putin in Moscow on Thursday afternoon and about an hour with President Zelenskyy and his chief negotiator, Mr. Umerov, at the Irish military airfield, in the Baldonnel account above. President Zelenskyy said: “Our soldiers will come home,” and called the exchange “a real result,” in the same account and in the Dublin account filed below. Later in the night he wrote that the week had produced three things: prisoners will be released in the largest exchange of the war; European representatives are being involved in diplomacy more actively, at the negotiating table on equal terms; and the next multilateral meetings are being prepared, in the Baldonnel account above. Mr. Kushner said the envoys were able to finalize on the prisoner exchange, spoke of returning thousands of people to their families, and later posted that both sides had agreed to expand the next round to include the European partners, in the Dublin account above. Mr. Witkoff said another meeting is on the schedule. No date, no place and no prisoner figure was given by any of the three.

On Europe, the night holds two accounts of the same Kremlin conversation, and the desk prints them at full size, as it found them. Mr. Kushner, standing beside President Zelenskyy, said of President Putin that he is willing to give it a try with Europeans at the table, in the Baldonnel account above. Mr. Ushakov’s statement, published the same evening, called the conversation substantive, constructive, frank and useful, said President Putin backed the initiative for another, apparently the largest, exchange, with its parameters currently being agreed, and said of the Europeans that they must decide whether they want peace or the continuation of the war, their practical actions so far pointing to the latter, in the same account. Mr. Peskov added that Europe must first name a representative, in the same account. In Dublin, more than 40 European leaders ended their summit without naming one: Ms. Kallas said the treaties give the seat to Mr. Costa, who chairs the European Council, and to herself; Chancellor Merz named the E3 of Germany, France and the United Kingdom, and a group of five adding Italy and Poland; President Macron said the format will be determined later; and Mr. Costa said work would continue in several formats, in the Baldonnel account above. The Coalition of the Willing meets in Berlin next week, the next occasion named in the file for Europe to fill the chair it is said to hold. Mr. Ushakov’s statement carried a second road and a reminder: President Putin reminded the Americans of the draft treaties Russia handed to the United States and NATO in 2021—no expansion of the alliance, no weapons systems near Russia’s borders that threaten it, and a return of the alliance’s forces to their 1997 positions—and the two presidents will continue discussions at the APEC summit in China, in the Baldonnel account above and the Dublin account above. Settled: the briefing happened, the next meeting exists on a schedule, and the exchange is agreed in the word of every delegation. Open: its number, its date, Europe’s name, the land and the ceasefire.

Nvidia at Midnight: Testimony Agreed Before Thanksgiving, Interviews Set for December, and a Third Allegation Printed as an Allegation

The company file stopped being a company file on Thursday afternoon and became a congressional calendar. Mr. Huang confirmed that he would testify in Congress at some point before Thanksgiving, which falls on November 26; the testimony is expected behind closed doors, and Chairman Mast believes it will be recorded and transcribed, in the timeline account filed below. The three House chairmen—Mr. Mast, Mr. Moolenaar and Mr. Crawford—wrote to Mr. Huang and to the company’s general counsel, Mr. Teter, requiring closed-door transcribed interviews on December 1 and December 2 respectively, or subpoenas to compel them, and asked Under Secretary Kessler to testify at a December 3 hearing, in the wire account at the top of this report. Senator Scott, the Senate Banking chairman, sent letters on Thursday to Mr. Huang and to Secretary Lutnick asking both to testify, said he would consider subpoenaing Mr. Huang, and wrote that recent reports raise serious concerns about national security and the protection of sensitive American technology, in the same account; the account adds that senior White House officials were separately discussing whether Secretary Lutnick should be pushed out, over the administration’s refusal to add dozens of Chinese companies to a trade blacklist and over oversight of the company’s exports to China. On the central allegation the file gained its first official non-finding: Attorney General Blanche said on Thursday that the Justice Department has not yet reached a conclusion on whether Ms. Alice Huang is a spy, China denied that she is, and Ms. Huang could not be reached for comment, in the wire account above. No finding has been made by the board, by any committee or by any court on any allegation in this file.

The afternoon added one allegation and one continuation, and both are printed with their sources attached. Reuters reported on Thursday afternoon, citing two people familiar with the matter, that Mr. Huang had an intimate relationship with another company employee, separate from the two previously reported; the employee is not named, and the company declined to comment, in the running account filed below and in the timeline account above. The same running account carries a report that the company will continue its internal investigation into its former chief executive even after his exit, and a Semafor report that multiple Justice Department probes could reach the company, with no indication the department would seek criminal charges against the company or Mr. Huang at this time. Ms. Kress’s memo to staff, seen by Reuters and carried in the same account, sets a company meeting for November 18 at 0900 Pacific, the day after the November 17 report, which stands as the company’s first under her hand in both jobs. The stock’s evening was quiet against its day: the after-hours price at 2000 ET stood at $167.87, up 1.01 percent from the $166.19 close, in the market data page filed below, and futures tied to the three main indexes gained between 0.2 and 0.6 percent in after-hours trade, in the daily analysis filed below. Settled: the resignation, the interim, the chair, and now the calendar—testimony before November 26, interviews on December 1 and 2, a hearing on December 3. Open: every finding.

Iran at Midnight: A Briefing on Further Strikes, a Friday Deadline in Congress, and Air Defences Over Tehran

The president’s Thursday sentences acquired a briefing behind them in the evening file. President Trump received a briefing from officials on Thursday on plans for a series of further military strikes to pressure Iran to negotiate, in the Tehran account at the top of this report, which cites Axios and its sources. Senator Blumenthal told a television interviewer on Thursday that his impression from briefings and other sources is that an imminent military strike is very much on the table, in the same account. Friday carries a date in the American file that no other day this week has carried: it is the deadline for Congress to approve the war, failing which—or a 30-day extension the administration must also justify—the United States will have to scale back its offensive significantly under the War Powers Resolution of 1973, in the same account. A senior administration official said late on Thursday that, for the resolution, hostilities had ceased with the start of the April ceasefire, effectively resetting the clock, in the same account. The two sentences—a deadline on Friday, and a clock already reset—stand in the file unreconciled.

Tehran’s night was spent answering in advance. Foreign Ministry spokesman Baghaei defended the closure of the strait on Thursday night as the defence of Iran’s right—legitimate, legal and accepted under international law, in the words the official agency carried—and justified attacks on American assets in Gulf countries, in the Tehran account above. Air defence activity was heard in some areas of the capital late on Thursday, one agency reported, and another said air defences were engaging small drones and unmanned surveillance aircraft, in the same account; no strike on Tehran is confirmed in any account in the file. A senior Guard official said any new American attack, even if limited, would usher in long and painful strikes on its regional positions, and the aerospace force commander is quoted that the Americans have seen what happened to their regional bases and will see the same happen to their warships, in the same account. The Supreme Leader’s written message said the enemies’ abuses of the waterway would be eliminated under the strait’s new management, in the same account. The United Arab Emirates said on Thursday it had banned its citizens from travelling to Iran, Lebanon and Iraq and urged those there to leave, in the same account. Both blockades stand. Settled: the positions, again, from every authorized voice on both sides, now including a date in Congress. Open: whether Friday brings an approval, an extension, a strike, or none of the three.

The War at Midnight: One Killed in Kyiv, the Injured Counted Three Ways, and a Service Described in Two Sentences

Kyiv’s Thursday toll closed with a mayoral total that gathers the night and the day into one figure. Mayor Klitschko reported on November 12 that one person was killed and eight others injured as a result of the overnight and daytime strikes on the capital, in the day’s account filed below—against five injured in the mayor’s morning account and the district account the evening edition carried, and two injured in two other accounts, all standing in the Cocked Hat. The dead woman stands in every account at 44, killed in the Solomianski district, where a drone struck a nine-storey building. The daytime incident stands as the evening edition printed it: a downed jet-powered drone on Olena Teliha Street at about 1240, a car burned, a bus damaged, a man burned on the arms. The day’s account adds that a Russian colonel was reportedly killed in a car explosion near St. Petersburg, in the same account above, which the evening edition carried from the wire without a name.

On the satellite service, the file did not move, and the desk records the standstill as a fact of the day. President Zelenskyy’s Thursday statement stands in full in the service account filed below: significant disruptions along the entire front line and in the occupied territories for several days, systematic restrictions limiting the system to 161 kilometres per hour, strikes that got through because interception systems cannot reach sufficient speeds, and Kyiv trying to establish all the circumstances with the American side. The company’s answer stands in the same account: this is false; there has been no change. The account itself says it cannot independently verify the claims. No American official has confirmed or denied the restriction in any account in the file through midnight, and the Dublin briefing produced no sentence on it in any account the desk read. The two sentences stand side by side into Friday.

The Markets at Midnight: The Closes Stand, Brent Prints Two Prices, and Friday Holds the Producer Figure

Nothing in the evening file moved Thursday’s closes, and the desk files them once, as the evening edition printed them, with the night’s additions beside them. The S&P 500 closed down 0.35 percent at 7,592.40, the Nasdaq Composite down 0.39 percent at 25,366.09, the Dow Jones Industrial Average down 0.36 percent at 52,297.09, and the small-company index down 1.66 percent. The 10-year Treasury yield stood at 5.10 percent, its highest since October 21, and the 30-year auction stopped at 5.441 percent. Europe closed at a record. Asia’s Thursday closes, which the overnight hours supplied, run lower across the chip markets: the Nikkei 225 down 0.70 percent to 60,819.36 in its first decline in four sessions, the Hang Seng down 1.26 percent to 24,008.55, the Shanghai Composite down 0.67 percent, the Taiex down 2.63 percent and the Kospi down 0.61 percent, in the global close account filed below. Gold hit a one-year low in the same account. Oil’s late prints stand in the Cocked Hat: Brent at $95.82, up 3.3 percent, in the global close account above, against $93.59 in the evening’s late print and $93.85 at midday—three prices for one barrel on one day, the official inventory build of 4.7 million barrels beneath all of them. Friday holds the week’s second inflation fact: the October producer price index, due at 0830 ET in the release schedule filed below, after Tuesday’s consumer print of 0.4 percent against a 0.3 percent forecast, in the preview account filed below; the International Energy Agency’s monthly report is also scheduled for Friday.

Spain at Midnight: The Campaign Opens on the Stroke, and Its Polls Open Divided

Spain’s file turned its page at the hour this edition collects. The official two-week campaign opened at midnight on Thursday, in the campaign account filed below, launching rallies, televised debates and canvassing before the vote on November 29. The decree the standing body validated by 35 votes to 34—the figure the campaign accounts give for the vote the evening edition printed as carried by one vote—returns to the centre of the campaign in the same account: eviction protections, two-year rental extensions and a 2 percent cap on rent rises. The renewal decree’s rejection stands. The polls open the campaign divided in kind, not in degree: most private pollsters project a PP–Vox bloc capable of an absolute majority, while the public CIS poll released at the campaign’s start forecasts a PSOE plurality and denies that bloc a majority, in the campaign account above. The first rally of the new campaign in the file is the Vallecas rally held hours before the official start, where Ms. Colau carried Thursday’s split vote into her opening sentences, in the rally account filed below. There are 1.6 million new registered voters, in the campaign account above. Settled: the campaign is open, the decree stands, the other decree fell. Open: sixteen days, and which set of pollsters is reading the country.

The Count at Midnight: No New Alaska Figures on Thursday, a Judge’s Refusal, and Two Tallies for One Race

Alaska produced no new count on Thursday, and its file’s only new paper is a judge’s. Superior Court Judge Matthews denied the Peltola campaign’s request for the names of voters whose absentee ballots were rejected, ruling the records cannot reasonably be produced at this juncture while officials are still counting, in the ruling account filed below. The race itself stands on two tallies, and midnight prints both with their sources. On the wire’s first-choice figures, Ms. Peltola leads Senator Sullivan by 4,250—118,926, or 49 percent, to 114,676, or 47.2 percent—with 245,470 ballots counted and about 84 percent in, in the ruling account above. On the Division of Elections’ summary report, stamped November 11 at 1747 and carrying all 401 precincts, Ms. Peltola stands at 121,487, or 48.73 percent, and Senator Dan S. Sullivan at 117,512, or 47.13 percent—a margin of 3,975—with Mr. Heikes at 5,426 and Mr. Dan J. Sullivan Jr. at 4,100, in the Division’s report filed below. The two tallies count the race at different stages of its own paperwork and are printed as they stand, not averaged. The next results release is expected Friday; ballots mailed from inside the United States must arrive by Friday, overseas ballots may arrive through November 18, the ranked-choice tabulation runs November 18 if no candidate passes 50 percent of the first choices, and certification is targeted for November 25. The Democratic caucus stands at 55, and Alaska decides 55 or 56. In Mississippi, the counties certify by Friday and the state on December 3. Settled: nothing new, which on a count day is itself the entry. Open: Friday’s figures.

The Rest of the File: Jerusalem Waits for Tuesday, the Articles Rest, and Kraków Publishes Nothing

No new published fact entered the Jerusalem file between the evening and midnight: the committees stand approved, the speaker vote stands for Tuesday, November 17 at 1600, Mr. Eisenkot’s mandate runs to December 6, and the government is unformed. In Washington the eight articles against Secretary Hegseth rest in the Judiciary Committee, and the House’s Thursday was given to the Nvidia letters. In Kraków no forensic opinion has been published. President Zelenskyy wrote in the night that Russia has struck Ukrainian energy sites more than 310 times since the start of November and that nearly 700,000 families are without power, in the Baldonnel account at the top of this report; the figure stands as his, attributed, with no second count in the file. The desk fills none of the space where the findings it waits for will go.

The Cocked Hat

Three bearings never give a point; they give a small triangle, and this paper prints the triangle. On Europe’s chair, willing to give it a try in Mr. Kushner’s account of President Putin, against must decide whether they want peace or the continuation of the war in Mr. Ushakov’s statement of the same conversation, with Mr. Peskov’s sentence that Europe must first name a representative standing behind the second. On who speaks for Europe, Costa and Kallas in Ms. Kallas’s reading of the treaties, the E3 and then five capitals in Chancellor Merz’s, and a format to be determined in President Macron’s—three answers and no name. On the prisoners, the biggest and the largest in every delegation’s word, finalized in Mr. Kushner’s, its parameters still being agreed in Mr. Ushakov’s, and numbered by no one: 1,000 to 1,200 a side stands only as President Zelenskyy’s figure of the day before. On Kyiv’s injured, eight in the mayor’s gathered total for the night and the day, against five in his morning account and two in two others. On the satellite service, systematic restrictions at 161 kilometres per hour in the user’s account against this is false, there has been no change, in the owner’s. On Brent, $93.85 at midday, $93.59 in the evening’s late print and $95.82 in the global close. On Alaska, a margin of 4,250 on the wire’s first-choice tally against 3,975 on the Division’s summary, in one race counted at two stages. On Spain’s decree, carried by one vote in the evening’s accounts and 35 to 34 in the campaign accounts—the same vote at two precisions. On the war’s clock in Washington, a Friday deadline under the War Powers Resolution against a clock the administration says the April ceasefire already reset. Against the triangle, the midnight’s single-valued facts are these: the envoys briefed President Zelenskyy for about an hour at Baldonnel on Thursday night, and no prisoner number, date or place was published by anyone; Mr. Huang agreed to testify before November 26, the House interviews stand for December 1 and 2 and the hearing for December 3, and the Attorney General’s department has reached no conclusion on the central allegation; Nvidia closed at $166.19 and rose 1.01 percent after hours; the president was briefed on further strikes and Tehran’s spokesman defended the closed strait on Thursday night; a 44-year-old woman was killed in Kyiv; Spain’s campaign opened at midnight with its polls divided; Alaska counted nothing new and its judge refused a list; and no Dublin name, no Tehran reply to the briefing, and no finding in any file stands in the record. Friday holds Alaska’s count, Mississippi’s county certifications, the producer prices, the energy agency’s report and Congress’s war deadline. The log turns.

The Clippings Filed With This Edition

Everything the desk read for the report above, clipped and filed as a bureau files it. Each item is stamped subjective—a source with a position, printed because it is useful—and described by what it says. The desk’s report is the only item in this edition stamped objective. 25 items.

Subjective
Silent Dossier — Ukraine peace talks: will Europe join the next round?

President Zelenskyy came out of an hour with the envoys on Thursday night at Casement Aerodrome in Baldonnel, west of Dublin, and said the coming exchange will be the biggest of the war and that Europe will be in the negotiating team at the next meeting. Mr. Kushner said the envoys had put the point to President Putin in the Kremlin a few hours earlier and that the deal cannot be concluded without the Europeans at the table; of President Putin he said he is willing to give it a try. Mr. Witkoff said another meeting is on the schedule and gave no date or place. Mr. Ushakov called the Kremlin conversation substantive, constructive, frank and useful, said President Putin backed the initiative for another, apparently the largest, exchange of prisoners, and said the parameters of the exchange are currently being agreed; on Europe he said the Europeans must decide whether they want peace or the continuation of the war. More than 40 European leaders ended their Dublin summit without naming anyone to take the seat: Ms. Kallas said the treaties give it to Mr. Costa and herself, Chancellor Merz named the E3 and a group of five, and President Macron said the format will be determined later. None of the three men at Baldonnel gave a prisoner number.

Subjective
CNN — Mr. Witkoff and Mr. Kushner meet President Zelenskyy after talks with President Putin, as Ukraine says Starshield restricted again

The envoys arrived in Ireland late on Thursday to brief President Zelenskyy. President Zelenskyy told reporters after the meeting that the talks of the past days had been very important, that they give hope the war will end, and that the prisoner exchange would be the biggest since the start of the war, calling it a real result. Mr. Kushner said really incredible post-war security plans were being worked on and that the deal could not be concluded without Europeans at the table, and later posted that both sides had agreed to expand the next round to include the European partners. Mr. Ushakov confirmed the trilateral talks would continue and appeared to play down the European assertion. President Putin said Russia had never objected to pursuing dialogue with Europe and wants the peace to be eternal. On Starshield, President Zelenskyy said the restrictions are not random errors but systematic, and the company that owns the service said there had been no change in its service.

Subjective
Eastora News — President Zelenskyy: our soldiers will come home

After meeting the envoys in Dublin on Thursday, President Zelenskyy said the exchange had emerged from two days of talks in Abu Dhabi, that Kyiv had discussed swapping 1,000 prisoners from each side, possibly 1,200, and that the final figures are still being settled; he called it a real result and said our soldiers will come home. The account says the envoys brought another development, that Europe could join the next round, and that Mr. Witkoff said President Putin had agreed to include the Europeans, while the Kremlin has not separately confirmed the arrangement. It records that no ceasefire or agreement on borders emerged from Abu Dhabi, that Moscow demands territory it does not control, and that Kyiv refuses to surrender it.

Subjective
LLM Odds — President Putin hears the American pitch to bring Europe into the Ukraine talks after the Abu Dhabi round yields only a prisoner swap

The envoys spent about two hours with President Putin at the Kremlin on Thursday, a day after the Abu Dhabi talks ended with an agreement in principle on a large prisoner exchange. Mr. Kushner said one aim of the Moscow visit was to win Russia’s blessing for European representatives to join the negotiations. President Putin drew a line on Europe’s other proposed role, calling any European troops in Ukraine after a ceasefire unacceptable. The account records that the last swap, on October 23, returned 261 Ukrainian service members and nine civilians in exchange for 270 Russian prisoners, that exact numbers for the new exchange were still to be announced on Thursday, and that President Zelenskyy said Ukraine will not give up occupied land in exchange for peace.

Subjective
TechCrunch — the unfolding Mr. Huang scandal: a timeline

A running timeline of the Nvidia case. On Thursday afternoon Reuters reported that Mr. Huang had a third relationship, with another, unnamed Nvidia employee, after his resignation. The timeline records that Nvidia confirmed in a filing on Thursday that the board accepted Mr. Huang’s resignation on Wednesday, that Ms. Kress will serve as interim chief executive while keeping her finance duties, that Mr. Jones was appointed the board’s first chair, and that later in the day Mr. Huang confirmed he would testify in Congress at some point before Thanksgiving, on November 26. Chairman Mast said the testimony is expected behind closed doors and that he believes the briefing will be recorded and transcribed. The timeline also carries the earlier record: the Justice Department has taken over the federal investigation into Megaspeed, and the three House chairmen first asked Mr. Huang for a closed-door briefing on November 5.

Subjective
Reuters, via KTWB — the Senate Banking Committee chairman calls on Mr. Huang and Secretary Lutnick to testify

Senator Scott, the Senate Banking Committee chairman, sent letters on Thursday to Secretary Lutnick and to Mr. Huang asking them to testify over recent developments at the company, and said he would consider subpoenaing Mr. Huang if he does not voluntarily appear. The account says a growing number of lawmakers have criticized Secretary Lutnick over the administration’s refusal to add dozens of Chinese companies to a trade blacklist and over oversight of Nvidia’s exports to China, and that senior White House officials were separately discussing whether the secretary should be pushed out. Separately, the chairs of three House committees wrote to Mr. Huang and to Nvidia’s general counsel, Mr. Teter, requiring them to appear for closed-door transcribed interviews on December 1 and December 2, or face subpoenas, and asked Under Secretary Kessler to testify at a December 3 hearing. China has denied Ms. Alice Huang is a spy, and Attorney General Blanche said on Thursday that the Justice Department has not yet reached a conclusion on whether she is or not.

Subjective
Reuters, via WNFL — the Senate Banking Committee chairman calls on Mr. Huang and Secretary Lutnick to testify

The same wire account in a second filing, carrying the House letter in full: the three chairmen—Mr. Mast of Foreign Affairs, Mr. Moolenaar of the China Select Committee and Mr. Crawford of Intelligence—wrote to Mr. Huang and to Mr. Teter requiring closed-door transcribed interviews on December 1 and December 2 respectively, or subpoenas to compel their appearances, and asked Under Secretary Kessler to testify at a December 3 hearing. Chairman Mast told reporters that congressional staff spoke with Nvidia on Wednesday night about a date and location for a closed-door briefing. Senator Scott’s letters to Mr. Huang and Secretary Lutnick are recorded with his sentence that recent reports raise serious concerns about national security and the protection of sensitive American technology.

Subjective
CosAnalyst — Mr. Huang resigns as Nvidia chief executive: what it means for the stock

A running file updated through Thursday afternoon. It records the close at $166.19, down 4.3 percent, on volume of about 737 million shares, with the market value ending just above $4 trillion; a Reuters exclusive, citing two people familiar with the matter, reporting that Mr. Huang had an intimate relationship with another Nvidia employee, separate from the two previously reported, with the employee not named and Nvidia declining to comment; a report that the company will continue its internal investigation into its former chief executive even after his exit; a Semafor report that multiple Justice Department probes could reach Nvidia, with no indication the department would seek criminal charges against the company or Mr. Huang at this time; Chairman Mast’s statement that Mr. Huang has agreed to testify before Thanksgiving; and Ms. Kress’s memo to staff, seen by Reuters, setting a company meeting for November 18, the day after the November 17 report.

Subjective
USA Today — Mr. Huang resigns as Nvidia chief executive amid the investigation

Mr. Huang resigned after mounting scrutiny over allegations involving a relationship and an investigation into whether he had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation, and Ms. Kress will serve as interim chief executive while the board begins a search for a permanent successor, the company said in a November 12 release. The account records that the shares plunged by more than 13 percent after the news broke on November 12, that after the Journal reported on November 11 that directors were preparing to remove him the shares fell about 8 percent in after-hours trading, and that the company has shed about $600 billion in market value in the week since the board investigation was announced. It records the board’s November 8 announcement that independent directors, assisted by outside counsel, would oversee an investigation into whether Mr. Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence operation.

Subjective
Orxial — Mr. Huang leaves Nvidia after 33 years

Nvidia announced on Thursday, November 12, that Mr. Huang resigned as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, and that Ms. Kress is interim chief executive and keeps her finance job until a permanent chief executive is named. The board said it will consider internal and external candidates and named Mr. Jones its first chair. The account carries the week’s prices: the shares fell from Wednesday’s $173.73 close to $158.78 by 2000 ET on Wednesday, down 8.6 percent, after the report that the board was preparing to remove him, and traded at $155.78 at 0900 ET on Thursday, down 10.3 percent from the close. Results stand for Tuesday, November 17.

Subjective
Finnhub — Nvidia Corporation: financial market data

The market data page for Nvidia. The regular session of Thursday, November 12 closed at $166.19, with an open of $151.01, a high of $167.14 and a low of $148.80, against a previous close of $173.73—a change of minus $7.54, or 4.34 percent. The after-hours price at 2000 ET on November 12 stood at $167.87, up 1.01 percent from the close. The market value stands at $4.07 trillion. The third-quarter figures are estimated for November 17, with earnings per share of $2.526 on revenue of $111.356 billion carried as the estimate.

Subjective
Market Briefer — the global close, November 12, 2026: Wall Street absorbs the Nvidia shock as yields break 5 percent

American stocks slipped about 0.4 percent as Nvidia absorbed its chief executive’s resignation and the 10-year Treasury closed at 5.10 percent, while Europe set records, Asia fell, Brent rose 3.3 percent to $95.82 and gold hit a one-year low, in this closing account. The S&P 500 fell 0.35 percent to 7,592.40, the Nasdaq Composite 0.39 percent to 25,366.09 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average 0.36 percent to 52,297.09. The account gives Asia’s Thursday closes: the Nikkei 225 down 0.70 percent to 60,819.36, the Hang Seng down 1.26 percent to 24,008.55, the Shanghai Composite down 0.67 percent to 3,655.83, the Taiex down 2.63 percent and the Kospi down 0.61 percent. It names Friday’s producer price index as the next signal and puts Nvidia’s fall from its October 6 peak at more than 30 percent, a loss of about $1.8 trillion of market value in five weeks on the wire’s calculation.

Subjective
Percy’s Perspective — daily market analysis, November 12, 2026

Thursday followed Wednesday’s rally with a volatile session that left the S&P 500, the Nasdaq and the Dow each down about 0.4 percent and the small-company index down 1.7 percent, with Nvidia down more than 14 percent at the open and closing at $166.19, down 4.34 percent. In after-hours action, futures tied to the Dow, the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq 100 gained between 0.2 and 0.6 percent, and Nvidia shares advanced more than 1 percent, as selling pressure eased following the resignation. The account carries Japan’s October producer prices, up 0.7 percent on the month and 7.1 percent on the year, and India’s October consumer prices, up 6.09 percent on the year.

Subjective
Al Jazeera — Iran vows a long, painful response if the United States renews attacks

Iran says it will respond with long and painful strikes on American positions across the Gulf if Washington renews attacks, and has restated its claim to the Strait of Hormuz. Foreign Ministry spokesman Baghaei defended the closure of the strait on Thursday night as legitimate, legal and accepted under international law, and justified attacks on American assets in Gulf countries. Friday is the deadline for Congress to approve the war; without approval or a 30-day extension the United States will have to scale back its offensive under the War Powers Resolution, and a senior administration official said late on Thursday that, for the resolution, hostilities had ceased with the start of the April ceasefire, effectively resetting the clock. The account reports, from Axios, that President Trump received a briefing on Thursday on plans for a series of further military strikes, and Senator Blumenthal’s statement that his impression is that an imminent military strike is very much on the table. Air defence activity was heard in some areas of Tehran late on Thursday, one agency reported, and another said air defences were engaging small drones and surveillance aircraft. A senior Guard official said any new American attack, even if limited, would usher in long and painful strikes on its regional positions.

Subjective
The Kyiv Independent, carried by EuropeSays — the war latest: Starshield restrictions return, President Zelenskyy says

The day’s key developments, November 12. Ukraine’s military is again experiencing significant disruptions to the Starshield system for several days, President Zelenskyy said, with restrictions limiting its operating speed to 161 kilometres per hour, on the briefings of the defence minister and the commander-in-chief. Hours after the Abu Dhabi talks ended, Russia launched ballistic missiles and drones at the capital and the surrounding area overnight. Mayor Klitschko reported on November 12 that one person was killed and eight others injured as a result of the Russian overnight and daytime strikes on the capital, and that in the daytime attack a car caught fire and a bus was damaged after a drone fell onto the carriageway in the Shevchenkivskyi district. A Russian colonel was reportedly killed in a car explosion near St. Petersburg.

Subjective
The War Zone — Ukraine says Starshield disruptions are back as the American negotiators meet President Putin

For the second time in a month, Ukrainian officials and military personnel are complaining that weapons using the Starshield system have had limits placed on the speeds at which they can operate, impairing the ability to defend against missile barrages, as the American negotiators met President Putin. President Zelenskyy’s statement of Thursday is carried in full: significant disruptions along the entire front line and in the occupied territories for several days, systematic speed restrictions limiting the system to 161 kilometres per hour, a significant complication in intercepting jet-powered drones, and strikes that got through because interception systems cannot reach sufficient speeds. The company denied the allegations: this is false, an official told the account; there has been no change. The account says it cannot independently verify the claims.

Subjective
Particle — Spain’s two-week campaign opens after the housing decree is revalidated and the polls diverge

The official two-week campaign opened at midnight on Thursday, launching rallies, televised debates and canvassing before voting on November 29. The standing committee moved to validate the housing decree that triggered the snap election, returning the measures on evictions, two-year rental extensions and a 2 percent cap on rent rises to the centre of the campaign. Most private pollsters continue to project a PP–Vox bloc capable of an absolute majority, while the public CIS poll released at the campaign start forecasts a PSOE plurality and denies the right-wing bloc a majority. The account records 1.6 million new registered voters and surveys showing younger men leaning right and younger women leaning left.

Subjective
Demócrata — Ms. Colau kicks off the campaign in Vallecas with a message to Prime Minister Sánchez

Ms. Colau chose Vallecas to launch her coalition’s campaign for the November 29 elections, at a rally held hours before the official start, in one of Madrid’s neighbourhoods with a tradition of voting for the left. The standing body validated the housing decree by 35 votes to 34—protection against certain evictions, limits on speculative practices and an extraordinary two-year extension for contracts that meet the requirements—while the specific rule on automatic renewal of rental agreements fell after the PNV joined the rejection. The outcome left a partial legislative victory for the government. Ms. Colau demanded more courage against rentiers and speculators and called for the November 11 housing strike’s momentum to be carried into votes.

Subjective
Reuters — Spain approves one of the housing decrees that triggered the snap election

The standing body of 69 caretaker deputies validated the broad housing decree by one vote—rent caps, a temporary ban on evictions and limits on corporate purchases of residential property, in force since its publication in early October—and rejected, also by one vote, the measure for the automatic renewal of rental contracts. The opposition’s arguments are carried beside the result: Mr. Feijóo’s pledge to repeal the decrees if he governs, and the argument that the measures reduce housing supply and push up prices. The official campaign for the November 29 election opens on Friday, and the housing deficit stands at about 750,000 homes on the central bank’s figures.

Subjective
Profilo Politics — Judge Matthews denies the Peltola campaign’s request for the names of voters whose absentee ballots were rejected

Superior Court Judge Matthews denied the Peltola campaign’s request for the names of voters whose absentee ballots were rejected, ruling the records cannot reasonably be produced at this juncture while election officials are still counting, and calling the timing of the request the worst possible. Ms. Peltola’s lead over Senator Sullivan holds at 4,250 votes—118,926 to 114,676—with overseas ballots still arriving and the ranked-choice tabulation set for November 18. The account gives 245,470 ballots counted, about 84 percent of the vote in on the wire’s estimate, the next results release expected Friday, ballots mailed from overseas arriving until November 18, and certification targeted for November 25.

Subjective
Alaska Division of Elections — election summary report, general election of November 3, 2026

The Division’s summary report, stamped November 11 at 1747, carries the Senate race with all 401 precincts reported and 251,094 ballots cast: Ms. Peltola 121,487 votes, 48.73 percent; Senator Dan S. Sullivan 117,512, 47.13 percent; Mr. Gerald Heikes 5,426, 2.18 percent; Mr. Dan J. Sullivan Jr. 4,100, 1.64 percent; and write-ins 800. The margin on the Division’s totals is 3,975 votes. The report is marked unofficial results.

Subjective
OilPrice — the official data shows builds in crude, gasoline and distillates

The Energy Information Administration reported commercial crude inventories up 4.7 million barrels to 414.4 million for the week ended November 6, with gasoline up 1.8 million barrels and distillates up 4.1 million barrels, ending five straight weekly withdrawals. The build ran against the draws the polls had expected.

Subjective
XTB — oil gains nearly 2 percent despite a sharp rise in American inventories

Oil gained nearly 2 percent on the day despite the sharp rise in inventories, Brent up around 2 percent and the American benchmark up almost 1.5 percent in the afternoon trade, supported by renewed geopolitical uncertainty around the American–Iranian position after the president’s statements.

Subjective
Bureau of Labor Statistics — schedule of releases for the producer price index

The schedule carries the October 2026 producer price index for release on November 13, 2026, at 0830 AM Eastern.

Subjective
Kalkine — how much could the November 13 producer price index move markets following a hot consumer print?

Friday, November 13 at 0830 ET brings the October producer price index, the next inflation fact after Tuesday’s consumer figures: overall prices up 0.4 percent against a 0.3 percent forecast, core up 0.3 percent against 0.2 percent. The account says a December 9 rate increase is priced as near certain, so the producer data may decide whether the central bank moves by 25 or 50 basis points, and that components of the producer index flow into the central bank’s favoured inflation measure. Japan’s producer prices, published this week, were up 7.1 percent on the year in October.

entry.title: Nvidia Closes Down 4.3 Percent Under an Interim Chief, Moscow Restarts the Trilateral and Disputes Europe's Chair, and Crude Builds 4.7 Million Barrels Against the Draw Expected
entry.summary: The evening file for Thursday, November 12, 2026: the day’s developments whole. Nvidia closed down 4.3 percent at $166.19 after falling as much as 14 percent, with Ms. Kress as interim chief executive, Mr. Jones as the board’s first chair, no reason given in the filing for Mr. Huang’s resignation, and the analysts divided between downgrades and a clearing event. The envoys reached Dublin late on Thursday after two hours in the Kremlin; Mr. Witkoff said the trilateral has been restarted, a new meeting set and European representatives will join, and Mr. Ushakov played the European sentence down. No prisoner number was published on the day the numbers were due. In Kyiv one woman was killed and five injured in the morning attack, a downed jet drone fell on a street at midday, and the company that owns Starshield said there had been no change in its service against President Zelenskyy’s account of systematic speed restrictions. President Trump told a radio interviewer it is possible he would resume strikes on Iran right now, and oil rose nearly 2 percent even as the official count built crude by 4.7 million barrels to 414.4 million, against a draw expected. Wall Street closed down about four-tenths of a percent, the 10-year yield stood at 5.10 percent, the 30-year auction stopped at 5.441 percent, and Europe closed at a record. Spain’s validated decree stands for Friday’s campaign opening, and Alaska counts again on Friday. Collected at 1800.
entry.content:
The Evening File — The Desk’s Report

Objective

Nvidia Closes Down 4.3 Percent Under an Interim Chief, Moscow Restarts the Trilateral and Disputes Europe’s Chair, and Crude Builds 4.7 Million Barrels Against the Draw Expected

The evening file, the day whole: a resignation with no reason in its filing and a stock that fell 14 percent and recovered most of it; a restarted trilateral whose European chair is asserted in one capital and qualified in the other; a prisoner exchange still without its number; a satellite service denied changed by its owner and described as systematically restricted by its user; a president who says no deal is needed and a strike is possible right now; and an official oil count that built against every expectation while the price rose anyway.

By Eunice, the desk · Collected and analyzed at 1800 ET, Thursday, November 12, 2026. This edition continues the log from Edition No. 37, the Midday Watch, collected at 1200 today, from Edition No. 36, the Overnight Watch, collected at 0400 today, and from Edition No. 35, the Midnight Watch, collected at 0000 today. Where the evening figures differ from the figures those editions carried, the difference is stated here, in the open, and the earlier editions stand unrevised, as a log stands.

The Evening in Brief

Thursday closed with its three morning questions answered in form and open in substance: Nvidia has an interim chief and no stated reason, the talks have a next meeting and a disputed European chair, and the official oil figures are in and built where a draw was expected. Nvidia closed at $166.19, down 4.34 percent, after trading as low as $148.80, in the market data page filed below; the filing gives no reason for Mr. Huang’s resignation and does not mention the investigation the board opened on November 8, and the afternoon’s analysts divided between downgrades to Hold and the reading that the exit is a one-time clearing event, in the downgrade account and the clearing-event account filed below. The envoys arrived in Ireland late on Thursday to brief President Zelenskyy, in the Dublin account filed below; Mr. Ushakov confirmed the trilateral will continue and played down Mr. Witkoff’s sentence that European representatives would join it, and no prisoner figure has been published by any delegation. In Washington President Trump, in a radio interview after his morning post, said it is possible he would resume strikes on Iran right now, in the interview account filed below. The Energy Information Administration reported crude inventories up 4.7 million barrels to 414.4 million for the week ended November 6, in the official-count account filed below, and oil rose on the day. Wall Street closed down about four-tenths of a percent, the 10-year Treasury yield stood at 5.10 percent, and Europe closed at a record.

Nvidia at Evening: A Close of $166.19, a Low of $148.80, and a Street Divided on What the Exit Clears

The stock’s day is the resignation priced in full, and then priced again at a smaller figure. Nvidia opened at $151.01, traded as low as $148.80—a fall of as much as 14 percent in the accounts filed below—and closed at $166.19, down $7.54, or 4.34 percent, from Wednesday’s close of $173.73, on the market data page above; the after-hours print at 1655 stood at $167.30, up 0.67 percent from the close, in the same page. The closing accounts agree on the shape: down nearly 12 percent in early trading in one, down 13.4 percent to $150.49 shortly after the open in the open account filed below, and recovered to $164.80 at 1141 Eastern, down 5.14 percent, in the recovery account filed below. At the low the company’s market value stood about $560 billion below Wednesday’s close on the open account’s arithmetic; at the close it stood at $4.07 trillion on the market data page. The two rivals named in the closing accounts, Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices, each climbed nearly 6 percent and led the index’s advancers, in the markets account filed below—the rotation the European accounts named in the morning, completed in New York.

The afternoon’s considered responses run in both directions, and the desk prints them as they stand. Truist cut the shares to Hold from Buy and its target to $174 from $346, arguing that the risk runs past the man to the company’s culture and to the possibility that its processors became accessible in China, and Craig-Hallum moved to Hold with a target of $180 from $275, in the downgrade account above; Bernstein’s cut to $200 from $400 and Baird’s to Neutral stood from the morning, and Oppenheimer cut its rating to market perform during the day, in the recovery account above. Against those, DA Davidson cut its target to $200 from $300 and kept its Buy rating, and said Ms. Kress is a steady hand, in the downgrade account above. Mr. Kuo of TF International Securities called the resignation a one-time clearing event: with Mr. Huang fully separated, he wrote, further congressional summons or investigations should have less direct effect on the stock, the succession is unlikely to affect product development and competitiveness before 2028, and Google’s processor stands as a near-term beneficiary as customers look for alternatives they trust, in the clearing-event account above. No finding has been made by the board, by any committee or by any court on any allegation in the file; the filing’s silence on the investigation stands where the midday edition left it, and Tuesday, November 17 remains the company’s first report under Ms. Kress, holding both top jobs, with the committees’ November 18 briefing still addressed to a man who no longer holds the office it was addressed to.

The evening’s new bearing on Europe comes from the Russian side of the table, and it qualifies the American one without withdrawing the meeting. Mr. Ushakov, the president’s foreign policy aide, confirmed that trilateral talks involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States would continue, and appeared to play down the assertion that European representatives would also join them: they are making every effort to get involved, he said, but they need to decide whether they want peace or a continuation of the war, and so far their practical actions point to the latter, in the Dublin account above. Who would represent Europe is itself unsettled: European heads of state will discuss the question on Friday at the informal summit in Dublin, no official decision on a special representative is expected, an understanding is possible, and President Zelenskyy is insisting the final choice be agreed with him, in the Europe account filed below. Open: the numbers, Europe’s chair in the form Mr. Ushakov will accept, the land, the ceasefire, and a date and place for the round the restart promises.
